claim: All four target agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, opencode) support MCP tools over stdio, making a single stdio MCP server the lowest-common-denominator way to expose Cartographer's ~20 tools.
evidence: Each agent's MCP config differs only in path/format (3x JSON mcpServers + Codex TOML [mcp_servers]).
relevance: Justifies building one MCP server instead of four native tool adapters.
title: MCP over stdio is the universal tool layer across all four agents
SKILL.md is an open standard read by all four agents

claim: An opencode plugin is a JavaScript/TypeScript module exporting hooks and a tool: map, not a declarative directory bundle; skills/subagents/commands are discovered from .opencode/ dirs, not from the plugin package.
evidence: opencode.ai/docs/plugins shows plugins as code modules; skills/agents/commands are separate file-based mechanisms.
relevance: opencode needs split delivery (code module + file fan-out) — highest packaging effort.
title: opencode plugins are JS/TS code modules, not declarative bundles
Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex use declarative plugin+marketplace bundles; Codex mirrors .claude-plugin

claim: Cursor subagents force-inherit ALL MCP tools with no per-agent tool/MCP scoping field; the only control is a coarse readonly:true write-lock.
evidence: cursor.com/docs/subagents Configuration-fields table lists only name/description/model/readonly/is_background; FAQ: 'Subagents inherit all tools from the parent.'
relevance: Cartographer's read-only specialists cannot be faithfully reproduced on Cursor; must emulate via readonly + beforeMCPExecution hook.
title: Per-subagent tool restriction is the hardest-to-port feature; Cursor cannot do it declaratively

claim: AGENTS.md is native project memory for Codex, opencode, and Cursor; Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md first and treats AGENTS.md only as a fallback.
evidence: Claude memory docs; symlink/@import bridge strategy with Windows symlink trap.
relevance: Ship AGENTS.md as source of truth + CLAUDE.md bridge; no plugin slot owns repo memory so installer handles it.
title: AGENTS.md is native for Codex/opencode/Cursor; Claude Code needs a CLAUDE.md bridge
An npx config-fanout installer is an established cross-agent distribution pattern

claim: Codex plugin structure has no agents/ slot; custom subagents live at .codex/agents/*.toml and are installed separately from the plugin.
evidence: Codex /plugins/build plugin structure lists skills/, hooks/, .app.json, .mcp.json, assets/ — no agents/.
relevance: On Codex, Cartographer's specialists ship adjacent to the plugin, not inside it.
title: Codex plugins have no agents/ slot; subagents install separately
Cartographer core already lives in portable Python stdlib + node strip-types CLI scripts
